episode_title: Kickstarting Marketplaces and Solving the Cold Start Problem

sections.dialogue: Lenny Rachitsky: In two-sided marketplaces, supply and demand are not created equal. In 90% of successful marketplaces (Airbnb, Uber, DoorDash, Etsy), supply is the constraining side. You must obsess over acquiring supply first, often through unscalable manual hustle: door-to-door sales, scraping listings, or offering financial subsidies. Once you achieve high-density local supply in one micro-market (e.g. NYC during a conference), organic demand naturally follows.

sections.topic: Good vs. Great Retention Benchmarks in SaaS and Marketplaces
sections.dialogue: Lenny Rachitsky: Looking at data across top tech companies, what constitutes Good vs. Great 6-month user retention? In Consumer Social, Good is 25%, Great is 45%. In B2B SMB SaaS, Good is 60%, Great is 80%. In Enterprise B2B SaaS, Good net revenue retention (NRR) is 110%, Great NRR is 130%+. If your cohort curves do not flatten out by month 3 or month 6, you must fix product retention before increasing marketing spend.
